p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting catabolic pathways for arginine, histidine, glutamate, glutamine, and proline. On the top left is arginine in a box. It begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2 (all Cs are pink), which bonds down to NH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to NH, and down to +NH3. To the right is an arrow pointing right, identified as arginase (in blue), to ornithine. Above this is a curved arrow pointing from H2O to urea. Ornithine begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to +NH3. All Cs are pink. To the right is an arrow, identified as ornithine delta-aminotransferase (in blue), pointing right to glutamate gamma-semialdehyde. This begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to H. All Cs are pink. To the right are reversible arrows with another arrow jetting up from the arrow pointing right to uncatalyzed H2O. H2O joins the arrow pointing left. To the right of these arrows is proline (in a box), which begins with +NH2, bonds left and up to H2C, bonds up to H2C, bonds right to CH2, bonds down to CH and bonds right to COO-. Below this is an arrow, identified as proline oxidase (in blue), pointing to delat1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate, which is the same as proline, but +NH double bonds up to HC (not H2C). Below this, at the bottom left is histidine (in a box), which begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to HC (all Cs are pink). HC bonds down and right to N, which double bonds right to CH, which bonds up and right to NH, which bonds up and left back up to C. To the right are four arrows pointing right. The first arrow, as step 1, has another arrow jetting up to NH4+. The second arrow, as step 2, has H2O joining the arrow. The third arrow, as step 3, is identical to the second arrow. The fourth arrow, as step 4, points to glutamate (in a box). This arrow has a curved arrow on top which points from H4 folate to N5-formimino and H4 folate. Above glutamate, there is an arrow pointing from glutamate gamma-semialdehyde, identified as glutamate semialdehyde dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right is a curved arrow pointing from NAD(P)+ to NAD(P)H [plus] H+. Glutamate begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), above to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to COO-. All Cs are pink. Below this is an arrow pointing down to alpha-ketoglutarate in a blue box. To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from NAD(P)+ to NAD(P)H [plus] H+. Also jetting off the arrow is NH4+. Alpha-ketoglutarate begins with C, which bonds up to COO-, double bonds right to O, and bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to COO-. All Cs are pink. An arrow to the right of glutamate points left to glutamate from glutamine (in a box). On top of this arrow is a curved arrow pointing left from H2O to NH4+. Glutamine begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus is over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to NH2.
